# payroll/

South African payroll: PAYE, UIF, SDL, ETI + run lifecycle, leave, termination/IRP5 prep, tax directives, UIF declarations. Pure engines have no DB; DB services are all company-scoped.

## Modules
- **Pure engines (no DB)**: `payrollTypes.ts`, `taxTables.ts` (TAX_2025/2026/2027; `getTaxYearConfig` THROWS `UnsupportedTaxYearError` for any other year; SA tax year ends Feb → March N ⇒ tax year N+1), `payeEngine.ts` (annual→rebates→medical credits→monthly), `payeAnnualPayment.ts` (annual payments, `payeTreatment`), `uifEngine.ts` (1%+1%, capped at ceiling), `sdlEngine.ts` (1% leviable, after the s11F retirement deduction; exempt <= R500 000 annual remuneration), `etiEngine.ts` + `etiTables.ts` (18–29, non-UIF-excluded, ≤24m employed; formula chosen by pay period), `payrollCalculator.ts` (`calculatePayrollLine` orchestrator), `validationEngine.ts`, `irp5ValidationEngine.ts`, `payrollJournalSplitBuilder.ts`, `payrollLabourComparison.ts` (the approval gate's labour comparison).
- **Run lifecycle**: `payrollRunService.ts` (CRUD + `calculatePayrollRun` populates lines), `payrollRunPeriodInputs.ts` (the review grid's once-off amounts, recalculated in the request; a #1117 writer: company lock, no write at all while the run's journal is in force (400, reverse it first), refuseAssignmentWrite on insert, inserts name `supersede_inferred = FALSE`, audited as `run_input` / `run_input_remove` (a removal is action 'delete' with the employee in metadata, which payrollRunRecalcGate reads); it reads what the run pays through the run's own reader, `payrollRunPeriodInputsRead.ts`; a cell save holds the company lock ~0.12-0.16 s on a 20-employee run (two whole-run calculations)), `payrollRunLock.ts` (period lock), `payRunApprovalControl.ts` (always-on R-035 clearance for the exact plan hash), `sdlLeviabilityService.ts` (SDL threshold basis), `payrollApprovalService.ts` (`approvePayrollRun` → approved + posts JE), `payrollJournalPostingService.ts` (`postPayrollRunJournal` / `reversePayrollRunJournal`), `payrollBatchService.ts`, `payrollBulkEmployeeService.ts`.
- **Employees + history**: `payrollEmployeeOnboarding.ts` (`createEmployeeWithPay`, POST /api/payroll/employees: judges every field and the salary component before the first write, then the employee and the recurring component in the request transaction; `EmployeeOnboardingRefused` = 400, raised only before the first write; `salary.amountCents` is integer cents, the column is rands, and `salary.amount` is refused; the salary component must be active, a taxable periodic earning), `employeeFieldRules.ts` (the tax and ID rules and `MAX_SALARY_CENTS`, DB-free so the form shares them; `irp5ValidationEngine` re-exports the validators), `payrollEmployeeService.ts`, `payrollEmployeeComponentService.ts`, `payrollEmployeeHistoryService.ts`, `payrollBankDetailsService.ts`, `payrollComponentService.ts`, `payPackageService.ts`, `payScaleService.ts`, `sarsCodesService.ts`.
- **Leave**: `payrollLeaveService.ts`, `leaveAccrualService.ts` (pure BCEA accrual), `payrollTerminationService.ts`.
- **Statutory**: `uifDeclarationService.ts` (UI-19 + `markUifDeclarationPaid`: DR 2150 / CR bank), `taxDirectiveService.ts`, `taxDirectivePaymentService.ts` (`applyTaxDirective`: DR labour, split and CC1-tagged as a pay run / CR 2140 / CR bank), `easyFileExportService.ts` (e@syFile EMP501 CSV).
- **Loans / costing**: `payrollLoanService.ts`, `payrollLoanReversal.ts` (undoes a run's own loan payments, tombstoning each on `payroll_loan_payment_reversals`), `payrollRunLoanApplication.ts` (`applyRunLoans` — reverse-then-re-apply in one locked transaction; refuses a run whose `journal_entry_id` is still set, in BOTH directions), `payrollCostAllocationService.ts`, `costCentreGlMappingService.ts`, `costCentreRunSummary.ts` (`costCentreSummaryForRun`: a run rolled up by cost centre, split by allocation; the master itself is `core/costCentreService`), `cashPayRegisterService.ts`.
- **Variance / duplicates / training / equity**: `payrollVarianceService.ts`, `payrollDuplicateDetectionService.ts`, `trainingEventService.ts`, `equityReportService.ts`.
- **Parallel-run comparison (Dotbiz Workstream C)**: `payrollParallelRunTypes.ts`, `payrollExternalCsvParser.ts` (pure; SA number formats → integer cents), `payrollParallelRunComparator.ts` (pure; IsaFlow run vs imported external payslips, per-employee per-component cent diffs), `payrollParallelRunCsv.ts` (pure CSV render), `payrollExternalImportService.ts` (DB; mig 495), `payrollParallelRunReportService.ts` (DB; assembles report).

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/payroll/*`. Every DB function takes `companyId` first. Pure engines accept plain typed inputs and return plain results.

## Main function signatures
- `createPayrollRun(companyId, input) / getPayrollRun(companyId, id) / calculatePayrollRun(runId, companyId, preparedBy?)`.
- `setRunPeriodAmount(companyId, runId, employeeId, componentId, amount, expectedAmount)` / `getRunInputs(companyId, runId)` (`PUT|GET /api/payroll/runs/[id]/inputs`) — `assertNotImpersonating` first. The row key is (employee, component, `is_recurring = false`, the run month's first and last day); the one row on it is edited whoever wrote it, 0 deletes. Rows are selected by the window the run pays (`getEmployeeComponents`' date): any once-off it pays that is not exactly on the key, or more than one, is `conflict: true` on read and 409 on write, because typing beside it would pay twice. `expectedAmount` is what the cell held: a mismatch is 409. Company lock, header lock, the row lock (bounded), every refusal (`PayrollRunInputRefusedError`), then `calculatePayrollRun`, the write and `calculatePayrollRun` again in one savepoint; a line this edit leaves further below nil than the first calculation did refuses inside it, so all of it is undone, and anything else thrown after the write is a 500 that rolls it back. `inputs.recurring` is what the run pays every month on each editable component. `isEditableRunComponent`: taxable earnings 3601/3606/3607; non-taxable deductions on `EDITABLE_LOCAL_DEDUCTION_CODES` only (company-local, never a four-digit SARS code or LOAN). No seeded catalogue has such a deduction, so the grid has no deduction column by default; the seed's Salary Advance is coded 3907, and any 39xx in a run's breakdown trips `lump_sum_without_directive`. A local code fails IRP5 readiness at year end (`IRP5_UNKNOWN_CODE`).
- `assertPayRunApproved(companyId, runId, expectedPlanHash?)` — mandatory reusable guard for every post/finalise path, including future payslip release, EFT export and `paid` transitions. It requires an approved R-035 request for the exact plan hash; only migration-951 historical approved/paid runs are grandfathered.
- `approvePayrollRun(companyId, runId, userId)` — status `draft|calculated → approved`, posts JE, links `payroll_run_headers.journal_entry_id`. Every refusal (not found, status, any journal-plan blocker via `judgePayrollApproval`) is thrown BEFORE the status write as `PayrollApprovalRefusedError` (its own module, `payrollApprovalRefusal.ts`); callers answer only that as a 4xx and rethrow the rest, so a post-write failure rolls back (K-079). Returns the plan's `advisories`.
- `judgePayrollApproval(companyId, runId)` (`payrollApprovalGate.ts`) — THE approval gate, used by `approvePayrollRun`, `previewPayrollApproval` (`GET /api/payroll/runs/[id]/journal-plan`, and the MCP dry run): status gate (`approvalStatusRefusal`, `payrollApprovalRefusal.ts`) → for a run linking a journal, by what its reversal chain leaves in the ledger (round 5, below): in force → figures must match (`recalculated_after_posting`, or `net_pay_target_changed` when net pay moved between the bank and the clearing account); out → replaced (with the `net_pay_target_replaced` advisory when its net-pay account differs from the reversed journal's; the dating moved to `payrollReplacementDating.ts`); unclear → `posted_journal_not_live` → else plan blockers except `run_not_approved`. Returns `{ plan, posted, replaces, blocker, planHash }`. `approvePayrollRun(…, { expectedPlanHash })` locks the header `FOR UPDATE`, then refuses a different hash with `PayrollApprovalConflictError` (route: 409) before any write.
- `postPayrollRunJournal(companyId, runId, userId)` — DR 5200 Labour = gross + (total_uif÷2) + sdl − etiUsed (split by cost centre: account by mapping, `cc1_id` = the centre); CR 2140 PAYE = paye − etiUsed; CR 2150 UIF (employee+employer combined); CR 2160 SDL; CR net pay (`payrollJournalBank#resolveNetPayTarget`, resolved once in the plan): the account holding the company's BANK system role (not the code 1110; no active holder is the `missing_bank_account` blocker, never a 1110 fallback), or, when Default Accounts' `payroll_net_pay` names one, that clearing liability (e.g. 2170) with the bank role not consulted (below); zero lines dropped. `etiUsed = max(0, min(eti, paye))` (see Business rules).
- `calculatePayrollLine(input): PayrollLineResult` — pure orchestrator.
- `markUifDeclarationPaid(companyId, declarationId, userId)` — idempotent (returns existing row when already paid).
- `applyTaxDirective(companyId, directiveId, input)` — one payment per directive.
- `computeExpectedAccrual(input): number`, `computeCarryOver(balance, maxCarryOver)` — pure leave helpers.
- `parseExternalPayslipCsv(csv): ExternalCsvParseResult` — pure; header aliases (VIP/Sage), comma/semicolon, SA amount formats; integer cents out.
- `compareParallelRun(isaflowLines, externalRows, opts?): ParallelRunComparisonReport` — pure; employee-number matching is trim/case/zero-pad-insensitive (numeric only); `uifTotal` compares vs ee+er sum; only components present in the external data are compared.
- `getParallelRunReport(companyId, importId, runId?)` — resolves the run by the import's period when runId omitted; `run`/`comparison` null when no run exists.

## Business rules
- **Pay-run approval (R-035, 2026-10-31).** Every existing and future company has a fixed, immutable `All pay runs` manager rule and enforcement row; there is no off switch or threshold. The last calculator is `prepared_by` and an approval request snapshots that author, so another eligible company member authorises it; R-035's audited sole-eligible requester exception remains. Every recalculation/reopen rotates `approval_revision`, changing `planHash` even when cents are identical. `approvePayrollRun` checks clearance for its locked hash before its first write; `postPayrollRunJournal` repeats the reusable guard. Reopen needs its existing >=5-character reason and clears the digest cache. Migration 951 grandfathers only historical approved/paid rows.
- **ETI in the journal (K-079, Hein 2026-09-26).** ETI offsets PAYE payable and is presented net of labour cost, capped at the run's PAYE: `etiUsed = max(0, min(total_eti, total_paye))` reduces both DR 5200 and CR 2140, so CR 2140 equals `emp201Service`'s `payePayable` (floored at 0; one run per company per period). ETI beyond PAYE is not booked and is reported as the `eti_beyond_paye` advisory; EMP201 carries none forward. Before the fix the labour debit fell by ETI while 2140 carried full PAYE, so every ETI run was unbalanced and could not post. The ETI formula is SARS' two-table schedule in `etiTables.ts` (K-080 closed 2026-10-18, see Recent changes).
- **Payroll journal plan = what the GL will accept (K-079).**
  - The balance check is exact to the cent. The cost-centre labour split ties to the labour debit
    (residual on the largest share), but only the rounding residual (half a cent per line). A
    bigger gap means the lines disagree with the header, and it is refused as `unbalanced`. ETI
    comes off the cost of the employees whose run lines carry it.
  - The GL poster's refusals are plan blockers (`nothing_to_post`, `negative_amount`,
    `closed_period`, `inactive_target_account`).
  - The deactivated-account check covers cost-centre labour accounts, resolved by id. It is not
    an advisory: `postJournalEntry` refuses deactivated accounts.
  - `approvePayrollRun` refuses every blocker before its status write. withAuth COMMITs a 4xx, so
    a refusal after the write stranded runs `approved` with no journal.
  - A run that already carries its journal (reopen keeps `journal_entry_id`) is refused by none of
    them, because re-approval posts nothing and returns that journal.
- Run state: `draft → calculated → approved → paid`. Re-approve is allowed when `status=approved` but journal unposted (2026-04-24 fix).
- JE posting: do NOT include `runId` inside `sourceDocumentId` (2026-04-24 fix — FK is to `documents`).
- Leave accrual INSERTs supply `company_id` for RLS (2026-04-24 fix); EXCLUDED out of scope in RETURNING clause (same-day fix).
- Employee active-check uses `payroll_employees.status`, NOT `is_active` column (2026-04-24 fix).
- **Run population is by end date, not status (audit 2026-10-18 P4).** `calculatePayrollRun` reads `listPayrollRunEmployees(companyId, period)`: every employee whose `end_date` falls in the run's month, whatever their status; active or terminated employees whose `end_date` is after the month (a run recalculated after they left); active employees with no `end_date`. `updatePayrollEmployee` still sets `terminated` on an end date of today or earlier; that no longer hides the leaver's final pay, leave pay-out and notice pay. Nobody whose `start_date` is after the month. Loan instalments are taken only from the run's employees (`RunLoanInput.employeeIds`). Termination pay-outs already paid in another run are not paid again (`payrollTerminationPaidCheck.ts`: `findPaidTerminationRun`, warning `TERMINATION_ALREADY_PAID`), and the approval gate refuses a run still carrying them (`termination_already_paid`, `findTerminationsPaidElsewhere`). "Paid" = approved or paid, or reopened with a linked journal whose chain is not `out` (a reversed journal stays linked, so the link alone is not enough; a linked journal the company cannot read counts as paid). `approvePayrollRun` takes a company-scoped advisory lock (`lockCompanyPayrollApprovals`) before the header lock so two such approvals cannot both pass; a second approver waits up to 5s, then gets the retryable lock-timeout 503. The posted-journal loan guard (`readRunLoanWork`, live and dry run) counts only the run's employees' instalments. `listPayrollEmployees` (active only; `{ includeTerminated }` adds leavers, for the directive form) is the employee list, not the run. Tests: `tests/integration/p4-leaver-in-final-run.int.test.ts`, `p4-leaver-run-edges.int.test.ts`, `p4-termination-approval-gate.int.test.ts`.
- **Employee bank details (wave 3 K1, migration 952).** `payroll_bank_details`: one active row per employee (partial unique index), a change deactivates that row and inserts the next. `setEmployeeBankDetails` takes the output of `parseBankDetailsInput` (all refusals before the first write), locks the employee `FOR UPDATE` (after the approval lock, see below), and only then decides first entry (owner / admin / manager) vs change (owner / admin, `CHANGE_REQUIRES_ADMIN`): any row, active or not, makes it a change. A manager's first entry is refused (`FIRST_ENTRY_REQUIRES_ADMIN`, 403, nothing written) for an employee who has been in any of this company's runs that was ever approved, posted or paid, in any period (Hein's ruling on D1, 2026-11-02): status approved / paid, `approved_at`, `reopened_at` or a non-empty `approval_history`, or a linked `journal_entry_id`; for a reopened run, whose lines may have changed, also anyone in `approved_taxed_employees` or employed in its period (so nothing taxable and a NULL set fail closed). Decided after the change rule. A caller who is not owner / admin first takes the company payroll-approval lock (`payrollApprovalLockScope`, the key approve / calculate / reopen use; an owner / admin is never refused by the first-entry rule, so takes none), then the employee row; so an approval cannot commit between the verdict and the insert. Both waits share one 5s deadline (503 `RowLockTimeoutError`: "Payroll for this company" for the approval lock, "This employee" for the row). The employee lock alone serialises bank-details writes for the employee. It is the service's rule only (RLS could state it but would not bind a forger of owner claims). Outside it: `tax_directive_payments` (pay outside a run) and an employee re-created as a new record. Bank name and holder take letters, digits, spaces and `. , ' ’ & ( ) / -`, starting with a letter or digit (422). The same details sent again write nothing, decided after the role check so a manager's PUT cannot confirm a guessed number; nor can `/api/payroll/duplicates`, which gives a manager no bank-account groups. `account_number` is full for owner / admin, else `…1234` (GET, PUT, history). For anyone but owner / admin, GET and PUT also mask `branchCode` to its last two digits (`…55`) and `accountHolder` to its first letter (`K…`; a value of two characters or fewer shows as `••`). `bankName` is not masked. This reduces, not prevents, matching two employees to one account: bank name + last two digits can give a bank's universal branch code, and last four + bank + type + initial can still match. The history masks the same three the same way for every role (`SENSITIVE_FIELDS` and `FIELD_MASKS` in `entityChangeMasking.ts`, MCP included); owner / admin see them in full only through the audited reveal (`entity-changes-reveal`, own session). `/api/payroll/duplicates` returns bank-account groups to owner / admin only, in full in their own session and masked to `…1234` in Login-as and token sessions; `findDuplicates` queries bank details only when called with `includeBankAccounts` (or `fullBankAccounts`) true, so omitting the option returns none. A full read (GET, duplicates) writes an `export` row in `audit_log` in the same transaction (`payrollBankReadAudit.ts`); its `revealed` names the fields shown in full: `account_number,branch_code,account_holder` for GET (from `SENSITIVE_FIELDS`), `account_number` for duplicates. The route's request log also masks `branchCode` and `accountHolder` (`maskBodyKeys`). Request bodies are logged only as scrubbed JSON objects, and query strings get the same key checks (`loggableRequestBody`, `loggableUrl` in `sanitizeRequestBody.ts`). The route refuses Login-as and tokens on GET too; MCP has no bank-details tool (census). No request role holds DELETE; rows go with the employee (FK cascade) or by `migration_admin` (the seed). RLS: owner / admin / manager read and insert, owner / admin update, and `is_active` is the only updatable column, so a stored number cannot be rewritten. `platform_admin` holds nothing and `app_service` has no mirror (915's exclusion list): a new reader must run in a request transaction. The history keeps the number in full (a reveal needs it), so 952 also puts `entity_changes` on 915's exclusion list: `app_service` has no mirror on it and a claimless service-pool session reads no row of it, whatever role it switches to mid-query (a per-row check failed there: a mirror's `USING (true)` is fixed at plan time). Every reader of the history (the routes, MCP, audit snapshots and comparisons through `runAuditTx`) switches to `app_user` with the caller's claims first and reads through `entity_changes_read`; a new service-pool reader must do the same. This closes accidental unscoped reads, not injected SQL: a claimless service session reads `company_users`, so injected SQL can forge each owner's claims in turn and read every company's history. No verification gate yet: it ships with the salary bank file (decision 6). Tests: `tests/integration/k1-*.int.test.ts`.
- Leave approver is the session user, never a request field (R-135). Every leave write route is `withWriteAccess` (R-136).
- VIP-parity foundations (2026-04-24): SARS codes table, bureau mode, period lock, variance engine.
- Cash-pay register, IRP5 certificate validation, e@syFile EMP501 CSV — SARS compliance export paths.
- `payrollRunLock`: once locked, period rejects new runs and edits.
- **PAYE by SARS source code (audit 2026-10-18 P3).** `payeTreatment` (`payeAnnualPayment.ts`): `3605` = annual payment, taxed by the SARS annual-payment method (G21 2027 p. 32–33: tax(annual equivalent + payment) − tax(annual equivalent), rebates/credits once, whole difference this month); `39xx` = lump sum, never taxed by the tables — only the PAYE on its directive (`EmployeeComponent.directive`), else `LUMP_SUM_WITHOUT_DIRECTIVE` and nil PAYE; anything else periodic (cumulative since G4, below). `PayrollLineResult.payeSplit` = regular / annualPayment / directive; `paye.monthlyPaye` is their sum; `taxableIncome` excludes lump sums. ETI base unchanged (whole gross). **Severance is paid in the run at its directive's figures** (`payrollSeveranceDirective.ts`, `payrollRunTermination.ts`): none approved → left out, `SEVERANCE_AWAITING_DIRECTIVE`; the first later run pays the leaver the severance line alone (`listSeveranceOnlyRunEmployees`: no salary, loans, UIF or SDL); directive ≠ calculated → paid at the directive, `SEVERANCE_DIRECTIVE_MISMATCH`; paid elsewhere → `SEVERANCE_PAID_BY_DIRECTIVE`. The run claims the directive AT APPROVAL in its one `tax_directive_payments` row (`payroll_run_id`, migration 901, no journal of its own; `payrollRunDirectiveClaim.ts`), so calculate/recalculate never consumes it, a reopened run keeps its claim, re-approval refreshes or releases it, and the stand-alone `applyTaxDirective` answers 409. Gate blockers `severance_directive_unavailable` (directive paid elsewhere, cancelled, or edited since calculation) and `lump_sum_without_directive` (a taxable 39xx component with no directive: no PAYE was deducted, and para 9(3) requires the directive before payment). The claim is taken after approval's last refusal. A claim is released only by approving its run again without the line (e.g. reopen → reverse the journal → directive cancelled → recalculate → approve); a run reopened and never re-approved keeps it, and nothing deletes a run. A leaver from an earlier period whose approved directive is not paid — unpayable figures (`SEVERANCE_DIRECTIVE_UNPAYABLE`), or severance already paid by hand as a 3901 in a run that has paid (`findHandMadeLumpSumPaid`, P4's `runHasPaid`) — has no line, so the reason is a non-blocking approval-preview advisory `severance_directive_not_paid` (`unpaidLeaverDirectiveNotes`), repeated on every run until the directive is corrected or paid, plus a `log.warn`. The repetition is deliberate (Hein 2026-10-22, G6 won't-fix): do not suppress it. Codes are classified after `normaliseSarsCode` (ASCII space/tab/CR/LF only), the same rule in JS and SQL. The severance-only line takes no ETI (`notEmployedInPeriod`: ETI is apportioned by hours employed, ETI guide Issue 5 §5.3). e@syFile also splits 3605 out of 3601 (`listRunAnnualPayments`). Lock order: approval lock → header → journal chain → directive rows (FOR SHARE) → payment row. Calculation takes no directive row; it only deletes stand-alone payment rows whose journal chain is undone (`releaseReversedStandalonePayment`) and holds nothing an approval needs after that. IRP5 data `lumpSums` and e@syFile 3901/4115 + 3230–3233 (`payrollLumpSumFiling.ts`); 3601 excludes them. Tests: `tests/integration/p3-*.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollCalculatorAnnualPayment.test.ts`.
- SDL leviability is an EMPLOYER test, not a per-line one: section 4(b) exempts total remuneration <= R500 000 over twelve months. `estimateAnnualRemuneration` bases it on the company's own trailing twelve periods (the eleven `calculated|approved|paid` runs before this one plus this run) using REMUNERATION — each run's `total_gross` (cash) plus its lines' breakdown items flagged `isNonCash` (the 3801 loan benefit), this run's `PayrollLineResult.remuneration` alike — divided by ELAPSED CALENDAR MONTHS since the company's first run, capped at 12, and by 1 when the window holds no prior run at all — so a seasonal employer's unpaid months count as zero, a company younger than a year extrapolates, and a dormant company resuming payroll is not spread over twelve months it did not pay; the 1% is then charged per line on `sdlLeviable` only. `sdlLeviable` is CUMULATIVE over the tax year's LIABLE months (`sdlLeviableCumulative.ts`; SDL Act s3(3), the leviable amount since TLAA 2017 (s3(4) is the exclusions; migration 957's comment still says s3(4)); SDL-GEN-01-G01 Rev 5 s6): to date = clamp(liable SDL-applicable pay to date − liable s11F deduction to date, 0, that pay); a line takes the rise over what earlier liable lines carried (floored at nil, cent-rounded; `sdl` is charged on that rounded figure, as `applySdlToLines` recomputes it). The deduction is PAYE 4c's own signed `retirementDeduction` from `calculateCumulativePaye` (4001/4003/4006, s11F: 27.5% and `retirementDeductionCap`), so SDL and PAYE take the same figure and there is no second cap or constant. A deduction larger than a month's liable pay waits for later liable pay, a reversal takes back only what liable pay absorbed (never above the year's liable pay), and a reversal-only or non-SDL-only line levies nothing. EXACT STORED STATE (migration 957, additive, nullable: `payroll_run_lines.sdl_applicable`, `sdl_leviable`, `sdl_exempt`): the writer (`replaceRunLines`, the only writer of the table) stores the line's SDL-applicable pay (`PayrollLineResult.sdlApplicable`), the leviable amount it carried, and whether the run was SDL-exempt (s4(b); `applySdlToLines` sets `sdlExempt` from `isSdlExempt`, the same test `calculateSDL` uses). `loadPayeYearToDate` sums ONLY the liable lines (`payrollSdlYearToDate.ts`: `PayeYearToDate.sdlApplicable` / `sdlLeviable` / `sdlRetirementDeduction`); an exempt run's pay, deduction and leviable amount stay out, so exempt months cannot be mistaken for liable ones (no heuristics). Breakdown items also carry `isSdlApplicable` (an earning flagged is_sdl_applicable, as costed). LINES BEFORE 957 (columns NULL, costed on gross) are read as costed: pay rebuilt from the breakdown (flag, else TODAY's catalogue: a later `is_sdl_applicable` toggle changes how those lines are read; `synthetic:termination` leave/notice pay by id; a deleted component counts nothing), exempt when the stored `sdl` is nil although that pay would have carried a levy of a cent or more (exact for them: no deduction reduced SDL then), leviable amount = that pay, and NONE of its deduction (Hein: no credit): the new rule starts with the first run after deploy and each EMP201 period stays right for its own month, so that month's leviable amount is its own pay less its own deduction. A later reversal of a legacy-month contribution is capped at the liable pay. REMAINING LIMITS: (1) a deduction larger than ALL the year's liable SDL pay, or recovered when no later liable month has any, is an over-levy that is not refunded or carried into the next tax year; (2) PAYE records one cumulative deduction, not whose contribution a reversal undoes: a reversal in a liable month of a contribution made in an exempt month counts against the liable months' deduction (an over-levy, never an under-levy). (3) A contribution capped by s11F in an exempt (or legacy) month has its catch-up recorded by PAYE on the next liable line, and SDL credits it there: an UNDER-levy, the only under-levy direction left (accepted by Hein; pinned by the "KNOWN LIMIT (3)" tests: R3 000 pay / R5 000 RA in an exempt month, then R60 000 liable: R558.25 against R600). A non-finite figure throws, and so does a year to date with earlier lines but no `sdlApplicable` / `sdlLeviable` / `sdlRetirementDeduction` (a hand-built one would silently over-levy; the loader always sets them). Every other taxable deduction (union 4018, medical 4005, garnishees) reduces neither SDL nor PAYE (calc version 4); donations 4030 only as `s18aDonation` allows. Like PAYE, it depends on which earlier months are approved when the month is calculated. The threshold stays on gross remuneration (`sdlLeviabilityService`: the header stores only total_gross). Tests: `sdlLeviableAfterDeductions.test.ts`. Never gate on the leviable subset — one component flagged `is_sdl_applicable = false` would exempt the whole employer.
- `calculatePayrollLine` takes `annualPayrollEstimate: number | 'defer'`; a run passes `'defer'` and sets `sdl` itself in the second pass.
- **Deductions and tax above pay (`DEDUCTIONS_EXCEED_PAY`).** `calculatePayrollLine` floors net at nil, as it always did, and reports the raw net (`ValidationResult.rawNet`); it changes no figure. A run carrying the code is refused by the gate (`deductions_exceed_pay`, `findOverdrawnLines`), because the residual the journal credits to 2175 understates what was deducted. Only on the fresh-journal path: a run re-approved onto a journal in force posts nothing. A due loan is previewed before any payment write: if all its instalments exceed the employee's available pay, or other deductions already leave no pay, the line carries `LOAN_INSTALMENT_EXCEEDS_PAY` severity error and only the non-cash 3801 benefit is injected. No payment row, schedule flag or balance change occurs. The approval gate, journal plan and MCP post, cash register and parallel-run CSV use the shared `loanInstalmentBlocker`; the CSV derives it from the same query that reads its run lines. Adjust or pause the loan or fix deductions, then recalculate to clear it. Exact equality is allowed. Only a line at nil is rebuilt; one at nil whose breakdown cannot be read is the blocker `run_lines_unreadable` (recalculate). A line from before the codes is judged from what it stored (`findOverdrawnLines`: gross less PAYE, employee UIF and the breakdown's deductions, rounded to the cent; LOAN from the breakdown's own code), never from the catalogue today. This is NOT a stale-input guard: a run whose components changed after its calculation (ended, edited, deleted) still approves its stored figures. `payroll_employee_components` has only `created_at`, so an edit leaves no trace without a migration.
- **Loan components (2026-11-02, Hein).** `loadLoanComponents` (once per calculation) takes the first active DEDUCTION coded LOAN and the first active EARNING coded 3801, codes after `normaliseSarsCode`'s trim. **No LOAN deduction fails closed:** a loan with an instalment above nil is withheld before it is applied (`payrollLoanWithholding.withholdingFor`): no payment, schedule flag or balance change; the line gets `LOAN_DEDUCTION_MISSING` and the gate refuses (`loan_deduction_missing`). **Two loan cases block approval until the follow-up PR handles them (Hein: a solution the codex gate accepts, with no GL or PAYE error):** a loan instalment above pay (`LOAN_INSTALMENT_EXCEEDS_PAY`, gate `loan_instalment_exceeds_pay`, naming the employee, loan and shortfall; way out: reduce or defer the instalment, close the loan, or pay final pay first), and a fringe benefit no 3801 earning carries (`LOAN_FRINGE_NOT_RECORDED`, the loan is still collected; gate `loan_fringe_not_recorded`: add the 3801 earning, recalculate). The follow-up: a cap at final pay (a migration), and the para 11(4) exemptions (casual loan up to R3 000, study loan) in `fringeBenefitOf`. The gate also refuses a run whose loan payments are not on its payslips as they must be (`loan_payments_off_payslip`, `findLoanPaymentsOffPayslip`: the LOAN item's component, by id, must be a deduction costed not taxable; a 3801 item of exactly the benefit must be an earning, unless the line warns for that loan). The run page's blocking list (`src/components/payroll/runWarningCodes.ts`) is held to the gate by `tests/integration/payrun-line-codes-census.int.test.ts`. A LOAN deduction is never a tax deduction: the calculator ignores `isTaxable` on a LOAN deduction (and records the item as not taxable; a LOAN-coded earning keeps its flag), `POST /api/payroll/components` refuses a taxable LOAN deduction, `list_payroll_components` reports an existing taxable LOAN deduction as not taxable. `setup-components` counts only what a run can use. MCP `calculate_pay_run` reports `withheld_loans` (dry: also loans whose benefit no 3801 earning carries, `withheld: false`) and, live, the `approval_blocker` the costing leaves. **The benefit is non-cash** (PR #1091, Hein 2026-11-03; design note heads `payrollCalculator.ts`): taxed (PAYE), SDL-leviable, in the ETI base and the SDL threshold, UIF by the component's flag (setup: off); not in `gross_pay`/`total_gross`, net pay or the journal; recorded as the breakdown item `isNonCash: true`. Only a TAXABLE 3801 earning carries it. **Filed under 3801** (Hein 2026-11-03; SARS PAYE-AE-06-G06 2026 Rev 13 / 2027 Rev 14 p. 16: low-interest loans are 3801, 3807 folded in from 2010): `payrollNonCashFiling.listRunNonCashBenefits` reads the flagged items; IRP5 data `fringeBenefits` (MCP `irp5_data` `fringe_benefits`), e@syFile income code 3801 after 3605 (cents dropped, nil left out), EMP501 CSV column `fringe_3801` appended LAST. `gross_salary` / 3601 / `gross_income` are cash; cash + 3801 = the remuneration taxed; PAYE stays 4102. A line from before the flag paid the benefit in cash, so it stays in 3601, and is SAID: `listRunUnflaggedFringe` → IRP5 data `warnings` (MCP `warnings`), the IRP5 summary row (`IRP5_3801_PAID_IN_CASH`, a warning) and ONE bounded e@syFile `X-IsaFlow-Warnings` entry (`unflaggedFringeSummary`: 10 names with amounts, the rest counted; pushed last so the header cap drops it first). e@syFile skips an employee with no income code of R1 or more (the writer's rule), with a warning (naming any UIF/SDL), instead of refusing the company — unless PAYE was withheld from them: then the export is refused (422) naming the employee and the PAYE, since 4102 would under-report. Other readers counting the benefit as remuneration (the flagged items added to cash): EMP201 `totalTaxableRemuneration`, the IRP5 summary's readiness (`totalFringeBenefits`), the journal's labour split (with a benefit in the run each line carries its own SDL, the rest by gross share, even with no cash gross at all; with none the gross split is unchanged), the run page (`nonCashBenefits` under Gross). The header's `total_taxable` is still written as cash gross: nothing reads it. Known limits: para 11(4) (above); a hand-made 38xx employee component is still paid as cash and filed in 3601.
- **Once-off components close at month end.** `getEmployeeComponents` (the reader `calculatePayrollRun` uses) filters on the `effective_from`/`effective_to` window and IGNORES `is_recurring`, so an open-ended row flagged once-off is paid in every later run. All three writers to `payroll_employee_components` — `postBatch`, `assignComponentToEmployee`, `applyPackageToEmployee` — therefore set `effective_to` to the end of the row's own `effective_from` month when the row is not recurring, via the pure `endOfMonthIso(year, month)` from `leaveAccrualService`. A caller-supplied `effective_to` always wins. Do NOT close at the batch/package period end instead: that bounds only the tail, so a backdated line still pays every month up to it (2026-09-09, K-025).
- **A package apply never cancels a hand-entered once-off** (`payPackageSupersede`): it cuts recurring rows and the once-offs the package itself wrote, by PROVENANCE: the row's creation audit entry says `package_assign` and, when it records one, this `packageId` (a rule on the entry, not on the amount, so an edited package line still replaces its own row); a row with no audit entry (before this release) is judged by shape (the package line's amount, closed at its month end). Any other live, un-superseded overlapping once-off (a back-pay, another package's) refuses the apply (400, nothing written, naming it). A salary closed on a day before the 27th pays nothing for that month, so onboarding refuses it before writing (`salaryEndRefusal`; `salary.effectiveTo` ends a salary before the employment does, and must then be a month's last day: only a row ending WITH the employment is read from the 27th). A package_assign audit entry that records no package vouches for nothing: the shape decides; the row's FIRST audit entry is the one read. Onboarding a salary ends with the employment (`endDate` closes the salary; paid months after it do not count).
- `applyPackageToEmployee` supersedes every assignment the apply OVERLAPS (`effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to >= effectiveFrom`), not only open-ended ones — once-off rows are inserted already closed, and an `IS NULL` predicate stepped over them, so re-applying a package in one month paid the once-off twice. A row starting on or after the apply date is voided (empty window) and the service warns naming it, because that silently cancels a future-dated assignment (2026-09-09, K-025).
- **A run reads components as at its period's LAST day** (`payrollRunReadDate(period)`, `payrollRunReadDate.ts`: a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' built without a Date; `getEmployeeComponents(employeeId, companyId, asOf: string)` binds it as given). Before, the run built `new Date(y, m - 1, 28)` at local midnight and the reader called toISOString(), so on the SAST host every run read as at the 27th and a once-off dated the 28th or later (including the batch UI's month-end default, R-006) was never paid. One read day for recurring and once-off rows alike: supersedes leave contiguous windows on one component, and two read days pay both rows of such a pair or neither. The last-day read pays a recurring row starting after the 27th in full and drops one ending from the 27th to the day before the last day, so neither passes silently (Hein 2026-11-02, `payrollRecurringProRata.ts`): the line carries `RECURRING_NEEDS_PRO_RATA` (error; component, date, "needs a manual pro-rata"; the run page groups it and says it blocks), and the approval gate refuses the run with `recurring_needs_pro_rata` naming each employee while such a row exists now OR the run still carries the flag (dates changed, not recalculated). No per-employee hold exists, so the whole run waits. Only lines that read components are judged (a severance-only leaver's line is not, in the calculation or the gate). Resolved with the profile's Edit dates (PATCH `/api/payroll/employees/:id/components?aid=`, open or ended rows; e.g. recurring from the 1st of next month + the part month as a once-off) and a recalculation; an amount-only change cannot clear it.
- **Assignment dates change in ONE place** (`payrollComponentDateEdit.changeAssignmentDates`; Edit dates = `updateEmployeeComponentDates`, End = `endEmployeeComponent`, REST and MCP `end_employee_component` with optional `cancel`). Under the company payroll-approval advisory lock (5s, `PAYROLL_COMPONENT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` → 503) and FOR UPDATE on the row and its same-component siblings, it refuses (400, `EmployeeComponentRefused`) a voided row; Edit: non-dates, end < start, a once-off open-ended or over two months; End: later than the current end (End only shortens), or before the start of a row a paid run read; an overlap with a live sibling; any change to what a paid run read (`payrollComponentPaidMonths`: approved/paid, or reopened with its journal chain in force; a supersede counts only if before that run's `calculated_at`); for pre-953 rows, a change that flips the inferred supersede. End CANCELS (voids) a row no paid run read when it is a once-off, the end is before its start, or `cancel` is asked. **Every writer is audited**: assign, End/Edit/cancel, package apply (each cut and insert), batch post write an `audit_log` row (entity `payroll_employee_component`, dates, kind, channel, actor; never the amount) in their own transaction (`payrollComponentAudit`). Assign, batch post and package apply take the same company lock first; package apply refuses to cut a row a paid run read. Tests: `tests/integration/payroll-component-*.int.test.ts`, `payroll-mcp-component-dates.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollComponentDateEditNoPay.test.ts`.
- **Once-offs inside the month and supersedes** (`getEmployeeComponents`, migration 953): a non-recurring row is read when its window covers the read date, or starts in the read date's month (10-27 Nov, the 28th alone, weekly overtime) unless `superseded_at` is set (package apply sets it, with clock_timestamp, on every row it cuts). A neighbour is NOT read as a supersede, except among rows with `supersede_inferred` (DEFAULT TRUE: rows from before 953 or written by old code); every writer here writes FALSE. A leaver's recurring row ending on their end date between the 27th and the month end is read for the whole last month (Hein), unless a live same-component row follows it the next day that is recurring, or any such row when a package cut it (`superseded_at`: the package's once-off replaces it) or both rows are pre-953 (`supersede_inferred`; a package apply that removes such a successor records `superseded_at` on the leaver row, `legacyLeaverSuccessorLost`); an earlier end date pays no recurring salary that month (as master). The pro-rata guard asks the reader which rows it paid (`assignmentId`), so a band row is always either paid or flagged. Edit dates refuses a superseded row. A multi-month window ending before the last day is not paid again in its tail month. Voided rows never. Every writer judges paid months COMPANY-WIDE by CALENDAR overlap (`payrollOnceOffGuard`, `payrollAssignmentWriteGuard`): assign, batch post and package apply refuse a once-off or recurring row dated in a month any approved run of the company paid (or a reopened run whose journal is still posted: remedy "reverse its journal"), whoever that run paid, and a once-off running past its month; a recurring insert (assign, batch post) also refuses an overlap with a live RECURRING row of the same component, as Edit dates / End do; a once-off is additive and never clashes (back pay, a top-up). Edit dates refuses only a paid month the row GAINS (it passes the row as it stands); a month it already touched is left to the employee's own paid runs (`paidPeriodChanged`). Onboarding with a salary refuses a start date in a paid month before writing the employee (`payrollOnboardingPaidMonth`, 400; `salary.effectiveFrom` puts the salary in an open month; no UI field yet). Census: `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollComponentWriterCensus.test.ts` pins the write statements per file, plus indirect writers and migration SQL, for `payroll_employee_components`. The batch post path is `payrollBatchPost.ts` (types and helpers in `payrollBatchShared.ts`, re-exported by `payrollBatchService.ts`).
- **Termination base = recurring earnings on the end date** (Hein 2026-11-02, `terminationMonthlySalary`): leave pay-out, notice pay and calculated severance in the final run, a severance-only run and the termination preview. A once-off in the leaving month is paid but is not in the base. Test: `tests/integration/payroll-termination-base-recurring.int.test.ts`. Tests: `tests/integration/payroll-run-read-date.int.test.ts`, `payroll-run-pro-rata-guard.int.test.ts`, `payroll-run-read-date-figures.int.test.ts` (a normal run byte-identical to master's), `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollRunReadDate*.test.ts` (2026-11-02). With a reason and a nil base (Hein): `TERMINATION_BASE_MISSING` (error) on the line, approval refuses (`termination_base_missing`), and `SEVERANCE_AWAITING_DIRECTIVE` is still raised (amount unknown).
- **Recalculation gates** (`payrollRunRecalcGate`, migration 953): every calculation stamps `calculated_at` (clock_timestamp, under the company lock) + `calculation_version` (`PAYROLL_CALCULATION_VERSION`, bump when a calculation change alters output). Every approval (also onto a journal in force) refuses a run without a current stamp (`recalculate_required`), one where a component audit row (clock_timestamp) of an employee on its lines OR in its population postdates `calculated_at` (`components_changed_after_calculation`, covers a hire added later; an end-date or termination-detail change in `entity_changes` counts too, scoped to the run; an unreadable history fails closed, `employee_history_unreadable`), and a `TERMINATION_BASE_MISSING` error. Paid months: a run without a stamp is judged by the 27th rule. Hand-built runs in tests must carry the stamp.
- Month-end must be derived with UTC accessors. `new Date(y, m + 1, 0).toISOString()` lands a day early east of UTC; `endOfMonthIso` uses `Date.UTC` (2026-09-09, K-025).

- **Cumulative (run-to-date) PAYE (PAYE 4a follow-ups G4) — a business decision, not a SARS prescription (Hein 2026-10-22).** SARS prescribes per-period tables for a full-year employee; G21 2027 p. 8's annual-equivalent formula is for a tax period shorter than a year, and G01 p. 5 accepts programs that "render the same results" — this does not when pay changes (it spreads the change, so can under-deduct that month; employer's risk, accepted). `payeCumulative.ts`: AE = periodic taxable to date × 12 ÷ periods with periodic pay; liability to date = tax(AE) × n/12 + [tax(AE + all annual payments to date) − tax(AE)]; PAYE now = liability − table PAYE already deducted, floored at nil and carried (no in-year refund); the annual-payment part = tax(AE + earlier + this) − tax(AE + earlier) (earlier 3605s stay in the base; G21 p. 32–33). Rebates/credits pro-rated by n/12. Unchanged pay (and any first period) = the ×12 result. A period with neither periodic pay nor an annual payment (severance-only line) deducts nil from the tables. Year-to-date: `payrollYearToDate.loadPayeYearToDate` — the employee's lines on approved/paid runs of the same tax year BEFORE this period (a reopened run, the run itself and later periods are out), directive PAYE excluded; each line stores `periodic_taxable`/`annual_taxable` (mig 913), a line from before 913 is split from its breakdown (taxable 3605 items). A month's PAYE depends on which earlier months are approved when it is calculated; the next month trues it up. A run calculated while LATER months of its tax year are approved (back-fill, or a reopened earlier month) is not refused: its taxed lines carry `PAYE_LATER_PERIODS_APPROVED` (`laterPeriodsWarnings`), since those later months missed it and, if February is among them, nothing trues it up. And a run is refused at approval exactly when its PAYE missed an earlier month, or a later month missed it and, for an employee both pay from the tables (periodic/annual taxable > 0), its line lacks that warning for that month (read off the lines per employee and month, as `laterPeriodsWarnings` writes it: jsonb containment on the warning's `periods` (YYYY-MM), never the message; a warning without `periods`, from #786 dev/test lines, reads as none: refused until recalculated) (`paye_year_to_date_stale`, `payrollYearToDateGate.judgeYearToDate` in the gate, under the company approval lock): recalculate it. Also refused (remedy: the LATER month — reopen it, approve this run, recalculate and approve it): a later month calculated from an EARLIER version of this run (this run approved then, per `approval_history`, its lines rewritten since) that pays someone from the tables whom an earlier approved version taxed (`approved_taxed_employees` UUID[], mig 925: the union over every closed approval, written by `reopenPayrollRun`; NULL with a history = reopened before the column, unknown, conservative, kept NULL) and this run no longer pays from the tables; the union is conservative for someone taxed only in a version that month did not read. A PAID later month is not refused for (it cannot be reopened): named limit (f), with an advisory. The remedy reverses the later month's journal only if its figures change (approval says so). Named limits: (b) the gate ignores how PAYE was computed — a run calculated before cumulative PAYE (lines without `periodic_taxable`) is judged like any other (refused if an earlier month was approved after it; otherwise approved with its ×12 PAYE, which the next month trues up, not February); (a) a NULL `approved_at` (pre-718) counts as approved all along, and a run that missed one is pre-913 too; (c) once the warning names a later month, the gate passes even if that month read this run's EARLIER figures for an employee still taxed here; (d) only approved months are judged: a month reopened and left (or cancelled) is in no pair until approved again; (e) callers with no outer transaction; (f) a PAID later month (legacy rows) keeps this run's old figures, said in the non-blocking preview advisory `paye_paid_later_month_stale`. The one-sentence rule and its completeness argument head `judgeYearToDateStale` (tests: `p4fu-r2-brk-employee-set`, `p4fu-r2-older-version`, `p4fu-r2-brk2-older-version`). "Missed" = the other month, as it now stands (lines no newer), was not approved when this one was calculated (first line's `created_at`); "approved at t" = current `approved_at` ≤ t, or t inside an approval a reopen ended (`approval_history` tstzmultirange, `[approved_at, reopened_at)`, mig 925; `reopenPayrollRun` writes it and `reopened_at` from one `clock_timestamp()`). The whole history, not the last reopen: two reopens leave a gap before the last one (p4fu-r2-exact-gate case 1). Runs reopened before 925 have no history → conservative refusal. All compared times are `clock_timestamp()`. Approve, calculate AND reopen take `lockCompanyPayrollApprovals` before their header lock, so nothing changes declarability between a calculation's year-to-date read and its first line; approvals, reopens and other calculations of the company wait (5 s bound). Kept company-wide, not per tax year (R2): 200-employee calculation p50 147–184 ms, max 233 ms at load ~38 (2026-10-23). Lock order: top of `payrollRunLock.ts`. ETI, UIF, SDL untouched. Tests: `payeCumulative.test.ts`, `tests/integration/p4fu-cumulative-paye.int.test.ts`.
- **Directive filing and integrity (PAYE 4a follow-ups, 2026-10-22).** A directive paid OUTSIDE payroll (`applyTaxDirective`) is declared by `directivePaymentFiling.ts`: EMP201 of its posted journal's month (`directivePayments`, in the totals; the route strips the breakdown for non-payroll-detail roles), and the certificate for that tax year (`listCertificateLumpSums` unions run and stand-alone; mig 901's CHECK keeps them disjoint). Only while its journal is in force (`payrollJournalInForce`). Codes: severance/retirement/death 3901 with PAYE in 4115; lump_sum 3907 with PAYE in 4102 (`lumpSumPayeCode`; G21 2027 p. 15, 21–22; BRS V25.3.0 p. 57). Apply refuses a directive not linked to a payroll employee (400) or not approved (409), and takes the directive row FOR SHARE. A certificate with no tax is an IT3(a) with 4150 = 04 (directive) or 02 (`buildEmployeeRecord`; `validateCertificateTaxFields` in `irp5ValidationEngine.ts` enforces the BRS 3015/4115/4150 rules). 3231 = `tax_directives.issued_date` (mig 912), else effective date with a warning (`X-IsaFlow-Warnings` on the e@syFile export, shown on the IRP5 page). A directive whose payment stands cannot leave `approved` (`updateTaxDirective` + `taxDirectivePaidGuard.ts`, 409; reverse the booking journal first); lock order there. The UI lump-sum calculator uses the SARS 2027 table (`src/lib/taxCalculations.ts`, `LUMP_SUM_TAX_YEAR`). Tests: `tests/integration/p3fu-*.int.test.ts`, `easyFileCertificateTax`, `lumpSumTaxTable2027`.

- **Medical credits: record, certificate, 65+ credit (PAYE 4a follow-ups round 2, R3, mig 926; Hein 2026-10-23).** Each run line stores `medical_credit` (4116), `additional_medical_credit` (4120) and `medical_scheme_fees` (deductions coded 4005, the calculator's `medicalSchemeFees`; employer-paid medical aid, a 3810 benefit, is not supported). A credit record = the credit inside the line's PAYE liability to date less what the employee's earlier lines of the tax year recorded (`payeCumulative`: used(x) from `annualTaxAfterCredits` `medicalCreditUsed` / `additionalMedicalCreditUsed`, weighted used(AE) × n ÷ 12 + [used(AE + A) − used(AE)]; `loadPayeYearToDate` sums the records). So a year's lines add up to the credit inside its liability; a line after pre-926 lines (NULL) carries their credit; a credit the liability no longer holds is a negative record; a severance-only line records nil. **65+ additional credit in PAYE** (`payeEngine.computeAdditionalMedicalCredit`): 65 or older on the year's last day, 33,3% × (annual 4005 fees − 3 × annual MTC), after the MTC, non-refundable (s6B(3)(a)(i), Fourth Schedule para 9(6); SARS Guide on the Determination of Medical Tax Credits, Issue 18, p. 21, 31-32; out-of-pocket expenses are excluded by the guide and not held). Cumulatively the fees to date are annualised over the pay's n (`loadMedicalRecord` reads them, a pre-926 line from its breakdown), so the credit to date is 33,3% × (F − 3 × MTC × n ÷ 12); the first month after earlier months without it takes the whole credit to date (floored at nil, carried). PAYE changes ONLY for 65+ with fees above 3 × MTC (golden grid `payeMedicalCreditIdentity.test.ts`, real-PG golden `p4fu-r2b-amtc-identity`). **Certificate** (`easyFileMedicalFields.ts`, `payrollMedicalRecord.ts`): 4005 (cents dropped), 4116 and, for 65+, 4120 only beside a 4005 value and only when the latest taxed month carries the record (else left off, `X-IsaFlow-Warnings`); a nil-tax certificate above the threshold is an IT3(a) with 4150 = 08 when a reported credit is above nil, else refused naming the missing 4005; `validateCertificateTaxFields` enforces BRS V25.3.0 p. 59-61 (`medicalFieldRules`, incl. 4120 against the age from 3080, else the ID number 3060). **Supported medical aid setup (round 2 review):** the employee's FULL scheme contribution is a deduction component coded 4005; an employer share is a separate taxable earning (IsaFlow has no 3810 fringe-benefit handling; the calculator processes earnings and deductions only, so `POST /api/payroll/components` refuses 'employer_contribution' with a 400 and the page no longer offers it, Hein 2026-10-25; the DB CHECK still lists it, and `component_type` VARCHAR(20) could not hold it anyway). Employer-paid or privately paid medical aid with no 4005 deduction gets the MTC in PAYE but no 4005/4116 on the IRP5 and no 65+ credit; the export warns (`medicalCertificateWarnings`), as it does for a 65+ employee (by ID number) with no date of birth (PAYE's age reads the date of birth only; not changed, a PAYE change). The 65+ credit needs scheme membership on the employee (beneficiaries > 0). `calculatePAYE.medicalCreditsApplied` stays the s6A credit only. Tests: `payeMedicalCredit`, `payeAdditionalMedicalCredit`, `easyFileMedicalCertificate`, `tests/integration/p4fu-r2b-{medical-credit,medical-certificate,amtc-identity}.int.test.ts`.

- **Only s11F and s18A reduce PAYE (calc version 4; Hein 2026-11-06).** Para 2(4) lets an employer deduct only retirement contributions (4001/4003/4006, s11F) and s18A donations (4030) before PAYE (PAYE-GEN-01-G21 (2027) Rev 1). Any other deduction marked taxable (4018, a taxable 4005, 4031, a local code) is paid from taxed pay and warned `DEDUCTION_NOT_PAYE_DEDUCTIBLE` (`payrollLinePaye.notPayeDeductibleWarning`); a 4005 still gives the medical credit. LOAN is never a deduction. Lines calculated before version 4 keep what they stored.
- **Donations (4030; mig 959; Hein 2026-11-06).** `s18aDonation.ts`, per SARS G21 (2027): a taxable 4030 reduces PAYE and SDL only if `payroll_employees.s18a_receipt_held` is ticked, and only up to 5% of remuneration after the retirement deduction, cumulative over the tax year (`donation_receipted`, `donation_base`, `donation_deduction` per line). No receipt: PAYE and SDL on all of it, `DONATION_WITHOUT_S18A_RECEIPT`. A reversal always counts. Lines before 959 stay out of the sums (no credit, no clawback). The full donation still leaves net pay and stays on the line's breakdown; the e@syFile certificate reports every 4030 deducted in full, taxable or not, whatever PAYE allowed (`RetirementContributions.donations4030`; G21 (2027) p. 11; a net negative year reports nothing). Every certificate with a 40xx/44xx/45xx value carries 4497, their total, after them (`withDeductionTotal`; BRS V25.3.0 p. 57). A reversal takes back only what counted, and what a line lacks taxable pay for waits for a later line. PAYE is costed twice (`payrollLinePaye.ts`) because the 5% is after the retirement deduction. The tick does not expire by tax year.
- **Retirement fund contributions (PAYE 4c, mig 948; Hein 2026-10-26).** Deductions coded 4001 (pension), 4003 (provident), 4006 (retirement annuity) are contributions BY CODE, whatever `is_taxable` (`retirementFund.isRetirementContributionCode`); they are capped by s11F; since version 4 no other deduction reduces PAYE (except s18A 4030). `payeCumulative` deducts the s11F amount before the tables, rebates and credits: D = lesser of contributions to date × 12 ÷ n, 27.5% × (AE + annual payments to date, both BEFORE the deduction) and `TaxYearConfig.retirementDeductionCap` (R430 000 for 2027, G21 2027 p. 5/10; R350 000 for 2025/2026, G20 2026 p. 5); AE becomes AE − D, so it is weighted n ÷ 12 (G21 p. 10 proviso); D beyond AE comes off the annual payments, never past the contributions to date (review #891). Donations (4030, s18A) are added back to the base (G21 p. 10: before ss11F and 18A). Year end = tax(remuneration − s11F deduction). The line stores `retirement_contributions` and `retirement_deduction` (the deduction inside the liability to date less earlier records, like the credits); `periodic_taxable` / `annual_taxable` / `taxable_income` are remuneration BEFORE the deduction (never negative; `validatePayrollLine` gets the figure after it). Contribution items carry `retirementContribution: true` in the breakdown. One rule for contributions, `payrollRetirementRecord.loadRetirementRecord`, feeds both the year to date and the certificate: a post-948 line's marked items; a pre-948 line's 4001/4003/4006 deduction items (today's components, named limit), with its taxable-flagged ones added back to periodic pay (the old calculator deducted them uncapped). **Paid outside payroll** (`payroll_components.paid_outside_payroll`, mig 948; a "private RA" the employee pays the fund directly): counted for the deduction and the certificate, but not in net pay, total deductions or the 2175 line (the journal's 2175 is the residual gross − PAYE − UIF − net, so nothing else changes); the breakdown item carries `paidOutsidePayroll: true`. Only a deduction coded 4001/4003/4006 (`retirementFundCodes.ts`, the one TS list): a non-boolean flag is a 400; CHECK `payroll_components_paid_outside_payroll_check` (code trimmed as `normaliseSarsCode`) and `POST /api/payroll/components` 400 (`paidOutsidePayrollRefusal`). Privately paid medical aid (4005, same shape) is NOT supported. Certificate: 4001/4003/4006 = the year's contributions per code, cents dropped, none when nil (`easyFileRetirementFields`, `payrollRetirementRecord`; BRS V25.3.0 p. 101-102). **Not supported (PAYE 4b):** employer contributions (3817/3825/3828 benefit + deemed contribution, 4472/4473/4475; 4474 is employer MEDICAL): an `employer_contribution` component is left out with error `EMPLOYER_CONTRIBUTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`; an earning coded 3817/3825/3828 warns `EMPLOYER_FUND_BENEFIT_NOT_DEEMED`. Tests: `payeRetirementFund`, `payrollCalculatorRetirement`, `easyFileRetirementFund`, `payrollComponentsPaidOutside`, `tests/integration/p4c-retirement-fund.int.test.ts`, `p4c-paid-outside-payroll.int.test.ts`.

- **Date of birth 3080 (2026-10-25).** Every certificate is nature A with a 13-digit RSA ID, and BRS V25.3.0 p. 26 makes 3080 mandatory, CCYYMMDD, correlated with 3060 and not after today. `buildEmployeeRecord` emits it after 3060 from `birthDate3080` (`easyFileMedicalFields.ts`): the payroll date of birth, which must BE the ID's date (YYMMDD; it gives the century) and not in the future, else the export is refused naming both dates (replaces round 2's 65-only `assertBirthCorrelates`: every age the export uses reads the payroll date, so it must be the one filed). With none on file, the ID's date; refused when that reads as under 15 at the year's end (ambiguous century: enter the date of birth). An ID whose first six digits are no date is refused. **Behaviour change:** exports with a payroll date of birth that disagrees with the ID, or an ID that carries no date, used to succeed and are now refused. `birthFromIdNumber` takes the latest century on or before today (was: 2026-12-01 for a 1926 birth). The route turns pg's 'YYYY-MM-DD' into a local day (`localDay`; `new Date()` read it as UTC midnight). `validateCertificateTaxFields` checks 3080 for 3020 A/B/C/M/N/R and refuses it on D-H (`birthDateRules`). Tests: `easyFileBirthDate`, `easyFileMedicalCertificate`, `p3fu-filing-edges`.

## Recent changes
- 2026-11-09 (wave 5 HD, round 1 fixes folded in): **hours and days per run for hourly and daily staff.** `PUT /api/payroll/runs/[id]/inputs` also takes `{ employeeId, quantity, expectedQuantity[, expectedAmount] }` (no amount, no component: either is a 400). `quantity` null clears the row, **0 is an entered nil** (stored: quantity 0, amount 0; migration 972 relaxes 967's `quantity > 0` to `>= 0`); `expectedQuantity` null = no row. `payrollRunHoursInput.setRunHours` prices it on the server, `amount = hoursAmountCents(quantity, rate)` in whole cents (`payrollRunHours.ts`), onto the run month's once-off Basic Salary (3601) row with `quantity` and `quantity_unit`. Everything refuses before the first write: a monthly employee (its stale hours row can still be cleared with null), no rate (400 naming it), no active taxable 3601 component, quantity above 744 hours or 31 days, a quantity that prices to under one cent, a stale `expectedQuantity` (409), a plain pre-HD once-off amount on the key (409 unless `expectedAmount` names it, then the hours replace it). A typed amount on an hourly or daily employee's Basic Salary is refused. The write is `payrollRunRowWrite.writeRunRow` (census pins its 3 statements there). The breakdown item carries `quantity` (number, 0 allowed), `quantityUnit` ('hour' | 'day') and `rate` = amount / quantity, the EFFECTIVE rate it was paid at (the employee's rate at entry, 4 decimals; omitted at 0): keys are omitted when no quantity was recorded, never 0 for missing. A rate raised later warns `HOURS_RATE_CHANGED` (cents only: under half a cent of total is not seen); the amount entered stays the pay. The line result carries `hours` (hours, or days x hours per day; null when unknown, never 0). Errors that block approval (`payrollRunHoursGate`: `hours_missing`, else `hours_inconsistent`, judged before the journal-in-force branch so a re-approval meets them): `HOURS_MISSING`, `HOURS_UNIT_MISMATCH` (a quantity row for another pay basis, e.g. hours left after a move to monthly), `HOURS_DUPLICATE` (two rows: never summed), `HOURS_WITH_OTHER_BASIC` (another row, recurring or plain, on the SAME component as the hours: paid twice; other earnings, 3601 or not, are ordinary pay). **The hours component is found by id** (`payrollRunHoursRead.hoursComponentOf`: the only active taxable 3601 earning, or with several the one named exactly "Basic Salary"; otherwise hours are refused 400 naming them, never a first match), and the validation reads the component the quantity rows sit on. A stored hourly or daily line with no quantity and no HOURS_* result, stamped with the current calculation version (two PRs bumping to the same number), is `recalculate_required` (`payrollRunHoursGate`; severance-only leavers exempt). An entered 0 prints "0 hours worked" on the payslip (`payslipQuantities`). A severance-only leaver is not judged on hours. A change of pay basis, either rate or hours per day after calculation sends the run back (`entityChangeQuery` WORK_TERMS). **Figure change (M2): until ET lands, an hourly or daily line under 160 hours, or whose hours cannot be told, claims no ETI** (`ETI_HOURS_APPORTIONMENT_PENDING`). `PAYROLL_CALCULATION_VERSION` 5. Tests: `payrollRunHours.test.ts`, `payRunReviewGridHours.test.tsx`, `tests/integration/payrun-run-hours*.int.test.ts`.

- 2026-11-05 (Hein, Velocity Fibre): **net pay can credit a clearing liability (2170 Net Salaries Payable) instead of the bank.** Velocity pays salaries by bank lines allocated DR 2170 / CR bank (47 in October, R803,850), so a run that credited the bank too counted net pay twice. New Default Accounts row `payroll_net_pay` (`app_settings.accounting_default_accounts`, a `gl_accounts.id` or nothing; absent keeps the bank, no migration, NOT a system role: 2140-2175 share the subtype `payroll_liability`). The rule is an ALLOW-LIST (`gl/netPayTargetRules.ts`, review round 1): an active, non-header LIABILITY whose subtype is `payroll_liability` after `canonicalSubtype` (so `payroll_liabilities` too), not 2140/2150/2160/2175, and (`gl/netPayLoanAccounts.ts`, a query) not named by any `loans.*_account_id`. Everything else is refused: a null subtype, `tax` (the VAT201 reads every `tax` line), payables, bank, credit-card, long-term and current-portion loan accounts. It is shared by the save (`gl/defaultAccountsService`: the 409 stale-page check, clearing allowed, an AUDIT row per change in the same transaction, and owner/admin only at the route, for `payroll_net_pay` AND `primary_bank` (the bank role it falls back to): a manager gets 403), the page's options (`roleCandidates`) and the resolver. The key names, the UUID pattern and the row parser live in `gl/netPaySetting.ts`; `parseNetPayAccountId` reads an object, JSON text, or a string written twice, and a row it cannot read is `invalid_net_pay_setting`, a BLOCKER (never the bank, never a throw); its text names the `accounting_default_accounts` row and says it needs repair by support, because the Default Accounts page cannot repair most unreadable shapes (non-JSON text fails the page's GET; `{"payroll_net_pay":7}` or a JSON list read as empty there, so Save has nothing to change). The generic `PUT /api/accounting/accounting-settings` accepts only four keys and refuses `accounting_default_accounts`. `payrollJournalBank#resolveNetPayTarget` reads the setting; in clearing mode the bank role is not consulted (a company with no bank holder still posts) and an unusable account BLOCKS (`missing_net_pay_account`, `not_liability_net_pay_account`, `not_payroll_liability_net_pay_account`, `header_net_pay_account`, `net_pay_account_conflict`, `loan_net_pay_account`, `invalid_net_pay_setting`, `net_pay_account_shared` (the net-pay account also carries another line of the plan, by id: a cost-centre labour mapping onto 2170 debited and credited one account; `payrollJournalBank#sharedNetPayAccountBlocker`), or `inactive_target_account`), NEVER falling back to the bank. The clearing line's description is `NET_PAY_CLEARING_DESCRIPTION` ('Net pay — net salaries payable'), deliberately not `NET_PAY_DESCRIPTION`: `foldNetPayBank` finds the bank credit by that text, and a shared description would fold a bank journal and a 2170 plan into one key and re-lock silently, keeping the double count. A reopened run whose journal in force went to the other target (or to another clearing account) is refused `net_pay_target_changed` (`payrollNetPayTargetChange.ts`, `payrollLabourComparison#netPayTargetChanged`); the text gives both ways out (set the setting back, or reverse: approving then posts to whatever the setting names at that time). A journal that was REVERSED and is now REPLACED carries the non-blocking advisory `net_pay_target_replaced` when its net-pay credit and the plan's are on different accounts (bank/clearing, two clearing accounts, a moved bank role): it names both and says the cash leg of the old journal stays where it was. An OLD journal whose lines carry no net-pay description is recognised by neither note: against a clearing plan it ends as `recalculated_after_posting` (a refusal, safe, less precise cause), and nothing re-locks. The account merge refuses to merge away the account the setting names (`accountMergeReferences#findSettingReferences`: the row is read and parsed in TypeScript, not cast in SQL; an unreadable row names nothing and does not 500). EMP201, UIF, directive and loan payments stay on the bank. Tests: `payrollNetPayTarget.test.ts`, `payrollFoldNetPayTarget.test.ts`, `payrollApprovalGateNetPayTarget.test.ts` (drives the real gate), `tests/unit/services/gl/netPay*.test.ts` and `defaultAccountsNetPaySave.test.ts`, `tests/integration/payroll-net-pay-clearing*.int.test.ts`, `payroll-net-pay-replacement.int.test.ts`.

- 2026-11-02 (payroll journal CC1, Hein: "post with CC1", NO backfill): **every labour debit carries the employee's cost centre in `gl_journal_lines.cc1_id`**, so budgets by CC1 see payroll actuals. `buildLabourDebitLines` aggregates by (account, CC1): an allocation row's centre, else `payroll_employees.cost_centre_id`, else untagged. The mapping still picks the account; an unmapped centre lands on 5200 and KEEPS its CC1; the global rounding residual goes to 5200's untagged bucket (created only when non-zero). Order: account, then CC1 (untagged last), 5200 last. `createJournalEntry` refuses a new CC1 that is not an active `cc_type = 'cc1'` centre (500, rolled back — verified), so `buildLabourLines` reads `cost_centres` and posts an inactive centre or a CC2 UNTAGGED on the same account with the `labour_cost_centre_untagged` advisory; a tag never blocks payroll (a centre deactivated between plan and post still reaches the GL refusal, as an account does). `PayrollJournalPlanLine.cc1Id` → `JournalLineInput.cc1Id`; the MCP `post_payroll_journal` dry run shows it (`DryRunJournalLine.cc1Id`). **Hash and gate**: `planHash` covers each line's CC1 (a preview taken before an employee's centre moved gets 409); after deploy every hash differs, so an open approve dialog or an MCP `plan_hash` taken before it gets 409 and re-previews — nothing posts on an old hash. A run approved-but-not-posted (legacy) posts the new tagged plan when re-approved. A never-recalculated reopened run still compares labour as a TOTAL and re-locks onto its old journal (tagged or not: the fail-closed rule below is for a RECALCULATED run only); a RECALCULATED one compares per (account, CC1) through `payrollLabourComparison#comparableLines` (pure; review rounds 1–2). The posted side is the journal AS POSTED: a CC1 changed by tag_journal_lines is read back from its first `dimension_tag_batch_lines.old_cc1_id` (`payrollApprovalGate#readPostedJournal`); when that earliest history is more than one row (two batches of one transaction tie on created_at — an MCP JSON-RPC batch — or one batch lists the line twice) the as-posted CC1 is unknown and reads as `AMBIGUOUS_TAG`, which no plan matches: a recalculated run is refused (fail closed, review round 3 T1). No labour line carried a CC1 as posted → CC1 is stripped from both sides only while today's plan is untagged too; once the plan tags labour the old journal cannot prove it, so it fails closed (d416d6de6: reverse and approve again; the `recalculated_after_posting` detail then says the journal predates cost-centre tagging — `payrollLabourComparison#predatesTagging`). An untagged journal with an untagged plan (a company without centres) still re-locks (`tests/integration/payroll-journal-cc1-untagged-relock.int.test.ts`). A raw SQL clear of cc1_id outside the tag tool is not seen. Otherwise the plan side is the plan's internal `labourBySourceCentre` (per account and SOURCE centre, untaggable centres kept apart; stripped from the journal-plan preview, not in the hash): a centre the journal carries keeps its id (deactivated since posting it still matches; a move between two deactivated centres still differs), another centre keeps its id if taggable now, else reads untagged; a taggable centre the journal does not carry is a difference (fail closed). The plan's `cost_centres` read is `FOR SHARE` (as the GL's check); lock order and why it adds no cycle: `payrollCostCentreTags#taggableCentres`. Reversal copies `cc1_id` (`reversalLines`, historical-copy mode keeps an inactive centre). Consumers unchanged: `payrollJournalChain` nets by account, `costCentreRunSummary` reads run lines, `glLineExportRows`/`autoPostingsModel` label the source only. Known, not changed: a centre whose net labour is negative gets its own negative line (refused as `negative_amount`; master refused the same run as `unbalanced`); the approve dialog shows one row per (account, CC1) with no centre column. - 2026-10-01 (W3-01 round 5, adversarial round on 25170a6fd): **a pay run's journal is judged by the LEDGER, not by `reversed_at`.** `payrollJournalChain.ts` reads the linked journal's whole reversal chain (journal → its reversal → a reversal of that → …) and nets its posted lines: `in_force` (nets to the journal; a lone posted journal always is), `out` (nets to zero), `unclear` (a draft in the chain, or no mirror). Three callers, one judgement: the approval gate (`in_force` → re-lock while figures match; `out` → `replaces`, a fresh journal; `unclear` → `posted_journal_not_live`, naming the journals), `calculatePayrollRun`'s loan guard (`journalInForceOrNull` — a run with loan work recalculates once its journal is out), and the generic reversal.
  - **`reverseJournalEntry` is payroll-aware** (`payrollJournalReversalGuard.ts`, called from the GL service, so the HTTP route, MCP `reverse_journal_entry` — whose dry run asks the same question read-only — and every service caller are covered). Scope: a pay RUN's journal (source `auto_payroll` and linked by a run, or described `Payroll run YYYY-MM`); UIF and tax-directive payments are not. Refused: reversing the last journal of a chain that nets to zero (it would re-book the run beside a later journal — approve the run again instead), and reversing the in-force journal of an `approved` or `paid` run (reopen first; a paid run cannot be). `reversePayrollRunJournal` goes through the same guard, so it too needs the run reopened.
  - **LOCK ORDER: run header → the run's journal (chain root) → each reversal in chain order.** Approval takes them before its gate reads; the reversal guard takes the same, in the same order, before `claimJournalReversal` (which locks only the entry being reversed — always the end of a chain). All waits are 5s. `reopenPayrollRun` takes the header lock too.
  - **Recalculated since posting → labour is compared PER ACCOUNT** (`runRecalculatedSince`: the run lines' `created_at`, stamped with `clock_timestamp()` at the insert, against the header's `lines_confirmed_at` — see the round 6–7 entries; the journal's `created_at` only for a run approved before migration 718). A recalculation can swap pay between cost centres and leave every header total alone; the split is then a real figure on a real expense account. A never-recalculated run keeps the totals-only rule (cost-centre/mapping/allocation changes and the old rounding cent are not the run changing).
  - **ACCOUNTING RULING NEEDED — the date of a replacement journal.** Implemented as recommended, pending Hein's decision (`payrollApprovalGate#datedForReplacement`): when the reversal that took the old journal out is not in the run's month (the month was closed, so the reversal was dated later), the replacement is dated ON THE REVERSAL'S DATE. Reversal and replacement net in one period; the run's month keeps the figures it reported; the later month carries only the correction. The preview says so (`replacement_dated_on_reversal` advisory, `plan.entryDate`) and the hash covers it. THE ALTERNATIVE: date the replacement in the run's own month — which needs that period reopened AND the reversal moved into it, or the month carries the run twice and the later month a negative (what round 4 did). Not implemented.
  - **Every chain walk is bounded** (`MAX_CHAIN_JOURNALS` = 25: both recursive reads carry a depth cap, the lock walk locks a row once and stops at the cap). Reversal links that loop (A reversed by B and B by A, a journal reversing itself) or run past the cap make the chain `broken`: the gate answers `posted_journal_not_live`, the reversal guard refuses, the loan guard treats the journal as in force. Tests: `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollJournalChainLock.test.ts`, `tests/integration/w3-01-forged-reversal-links.int.test.ts`.
  - `planHash` now covers run id, entry date and description (two months with equal figures shared a hash). The two scripts that call calculate/approve directly run them in `withAlsTransaction`, so the header lock holds.
  - Known, not fixed here: `POST /api/payroll/runs` has no `withWriteAccess` (a viewer can create a run); the GL's entry-number race (`uq_gl_je_company_entry_number`) still turns one of two simultaneous postings into a 500 that rolls back.
  - Tests: `tests/integration/brkr-c1…c7*.int.test.ts` (the adversarial repros, ported), `w3-01-reversed-journal-reapprove`, `w3-01-approve-approve-race`, `w3-01-calculate-approve-race`.
