- 2026-11-05 (post_payroll_journal double post + gate retag): **`postPayrollRunJournal` and the MCP `post_payroll_journal` live path lock the run header (`lockPayrollRunHeader`, level 2 of `payrollRunLock`'s order, 5s then a retryable refusal) before reading the plan**, and the final `journal_entry_id` stamp is `AND journal_entry_id IS NULL RETURNING` (0 rows throws, so a request rolls the journal back). Before, the idempotency key serialised only calls sharing it: two posts under different keys, or a post beside `approvePayrollRun` of an 'approved' run with no journal, each posted a journal and the later UPDATE orphaned the first. Behind the lock the plan reads the winner's link and the post is refused (`already_posted`); the poster also refuses a locked link its plan did not see. Dry run takes no lock but judges the same things (`readApprovedPlan`, `payrollApprovedPlan.ts`: approved, plan hash-matched to the approved plan, else both refuse). Lock order: the live post (and the poster when handed no plan) takes the company approval lock (level 1) and then the header (level 2) inside `readApprovedPlan`, then creates a journal (numbering); it does not take the chain (level 3). Two posting batches therefore queue on the level-1 lock for the whole transaction of the first (no deadlock; the second is told the run already posted); a batch that created a journal WITHOUT the approval lock (a manual journal, say) and then posts is the inversion below. **The journal-numbering advisory lock (company + year, taken when a journal is created, held to the end of the transaction) is the LAST level of every run writer's order (1 approval lock, 2 header, 3 chain/directives, 4 numbering).** One exception: a JSON-RPC batch to `/api/mcp` runs in ONE transaction, so a call that created a journal still holds the numbering lock when the next call takes the approval lock and another run's header, and a second batch holding those locks and waiting for numbering deadlocks it (40P01). Not fixable by ordering (the batch's element order is the caller's); the victim is answered CENTRALLY: the MCP registry's `thrownToolErrorText` maps any raw 40P01 (`deadlockErrorText`, `src/lib/mcp/lockWaitError.ts`, next to the 55P03 text) to a retryable refusal for EVERY tool (`post_payroll_journal`, `approve_pay_run`'s own approval/header/journal locks, anything else), shows no driver text (the registry's catch logs the driver error once, with the tool name); the HTTP routes already answer it 503 + Retry-After (`respondIfLockTimeout`, pinned for payroll approve in `tests/unit/api/payrollApproveRoute.test.ts`). There is no payroll-specific deadlock class: one mechanism. The retry on its own succeeds. A victim's batch may carry on (its transaction is usable: `sql` runs each statement in its own savepoint), but Postgres keeps the row lock a rolled-back, already-released savepoint took on a run header queued until the batch's transaction ends, so a victim that goes on to take the numbering lock again deadlocks the survivor a second time. Tests: `tests/integration/payroll-mcp-batch-deadlock.int.test.ts` (through the real registry), `tests/unit/mcp/deadlockRegistry.test.ts`. A caller with no request transaction (script) keeps the lock only for its own statement; the conditional UPDATE is then the only guard and cannot un-post the journal. **Gate**: for a run NOT recalculated since posting, `payrollLabourComparison#figures` no longer keys a line by cost centre, so a CC1 put on a credit line (2175, any) by tag_journal_lines after posting is not `recalculated_after_posting`; a recalculated run still compares per (account, CC1). Tests: `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollJournalPosterLock.test.ts`, `tests/unit/mcp/payrollTools.test.ts`, `payrollLabourComparison.test.ts`, `tests/integration/payroll-mcp-post-lock.int.test.ts`, `payroll-reapprove-credit-retag.int.test.ts`.
- 2026-11-05: net pay credits the BANK-role holder, not the literal 1110 (Velocity Fibre moved the role to 1544331 on 2026-10-27 and 1110 cannot be reactivated, so the October run carried `inactive_target_account` for good). `REQUIRED_PAYROLL_ACCOUNT_CODES` is now 5200/2140/2150/2160. The holder is judged by `gl/bankRoleHolder#resolveBankRoleHolder` (one source of truth, also used by the UIF, SARS directive and loan payments): `getSystemAccount`, then a fresh read of the chart (`systemRoleCoverage#readRoleClaimants`, not the 60 s resolver cache) so a role that moved within the cache window is `missing_bank_account`; two active claimants are `ambiguous_bank_account` naming both; a holder that is not an asset (a credit card carrying the bank subtype) is `not_asset_bank_account`; a header holder is `header_bank_account` (the poster's own `assertNoHeaderAccountLines`); a holder deactivated since the cache filled stays `inactive_target_account`. Re-approving a reopened run onto a journal in force compares net pay's bank credit as ONE role by amount (`payrollLabourComparison#foldNetPayBank`; exactly ONE posted line is folded, the one whose `gl_journal_lines.description` is `NET_PAY_DESCRIPTION`, so a credit the recalculated plan dropped — PAYE, UIF, SDL, 2175 gone to zero — stays keyed by its account and is a difference; a journal with no such single line is compared account by account): an unchanged run re-locks onto its posted journal and posts nothing after the role moved or lost its holder; a changed net amount (or any other changed credit) is still `recalculated_after_posting`. `uifPaymentService`, `taxDirectivePaymentService` and `loans/loanPaymentService` default to the same holder when no `bankAccountId` is supplied, and check a supplied one (`gl/paymentBankAccount#resolvePaymentBankAccount`: an active, postable bank-subtype ASSET account of the company); a refusal is `BankAccountRefusedError`, raised before the claim each takes AND before any write, answered 400 by the three routes (an already-paid UIF declaration and an already-applied directive are answered as before, without consulting the bank; a UIF declaration that is not `submitted` gets the status error (`UifDeclarationNotSubmittedError`, answered 409 by the UIF route) ahead of the bank refusal, read-only; `applyTaxDirective` reads the reversed stand-alone payments (`taxDirectivePaidGuard#reversedStandalonePayments`), ignores them in the already-applied check, resolves the bank, and only then releases them (`releaseReversedStandalonePayment`, the first write); a loan's stored `bank_account_id` is checked for company, asset type, active and postable but NOT for subtype, see `loans/.claude.md`). Pinned by `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollApprovalGateJournalReads.test.ts` (the gate's `l.description` select and its asPosted / current choice) and `payroll-payment-bank-role.int.test.ts`. The bank blocker is raised only when a net-pay line survives (net pay non-zero). `payrollJournalBlockers.ts` holds the blockers that depend on the finished lines (split from the builder for the 300-line cap); `negative_amount` names a line with no account by its description. The MCP `post_payroll_journal` posts the plan it reported (`opts.plan`), so the bank role is read once.
- 2026-11-05 (net pay review round 2): `upsertCostCentreGlMapping` accepts only an EXPENSE account (400 otherwise); mappings stored before that check are caught by the plan's `net_pay_account_shared` blocker. Unit-test fixture shared by `payrollNetPayTarget*.test.ts`: `tests/helpers/netPayPlanRig.ts`.
- 2026-11-05 (net pay review round 3): a journal in force whose plan's CLEARING net-pay line has no account (the setting names an account that now fails the rules) shows the plan's own net-pay blocker (`payrollNetPayTargetChange#unresolvedNetPayBlocker`), not `net_pay_target_changed` and not `recalculated_after_posting`; `netPayTargetChanged` is false for it. A BANK plan with no holder still re-locks (the bank role is one role on both sides).
- 2026-11-05 (R-035 follow-ups): `payroll_run_headers.approved_by` is the person who DECIDED the approval (`approval_requests.decided_by`, `payRunDecision#readPayRunDecision`, chosen by the hash the gate cleared), no longer whoever pressed POST /approve; the executor is the audit actor of the run's `executed` event, which also carries `decidedBy`/`requestedBy`. No decision to read (enforcement off) leaves the executor. **Sole-approver fallback (decision Q2, kept):** a requester who is the only member able to approve may approve their own run; that is recorded as `selfApproval: 'sole_approver'` on the pay run's `authorised` and `executed` events (the generic `approval_request` audit row already carried it) and returned by `GET /api/payroll/runs/[id]` as `approvalDecision: { selfApprovedSoleApprover, preparedByDecider }` only (`describePayRunDecision`; no ids, no top-level duplicate), with a note on the run page (`SelfApprovedNote`). `memberWrites` (role change/removal on `/api/accounting/company-users`) refuses with 409 to demote or remove the last other eligible approver of a PENDING pay_run request (`core/payRunApproverGuard.ts`; eligible = good standing, rank >= the ratcheted demand, not the requester and not an author: the run's `prepared_by`, `content_authors`; judged by PERSON, a case-variant row of the target is never another approver; TypeScript ranks: migration_admin cannot execute the SQL rank helpers). Limit: a demotion made before a request is raised is in the request's roster snapshot and is not stopped; a requester can also withdraw their own request and then demote. One judgement (`payRunApproverGuard`) serves every path that can take an approver away by a role change or removal: the company route (`memberWrites`) and the platform-admin link role change and removal (`companyMembershipService`, 409 `PAY_RUN_APPROVER`), plus onboarding reset (`adminUserActionsService`). The check takes the transaction-scoped advisory lock `pay_run_approvers:<company id>` on the SAME transaction as the write (held to COMMIT; platform writes lock on the request's `sql` transaction and judge on a migration_admin connection), so two concurrent demotions of the two other approvers cannot both pass; it is a leaf in `payrollRunLock`'s order (nothing in pay-run, approval or posting code takes it; taken after the member rows and the owner lock; companies in id order). **Suspension and user deletion are NEVER refused** (emergency revocation): they still land, log a warning and put the stranded request ids on the admin audit row (`stranded_pay_run_requests`); the requester still cannot self-approve that request, because the sole-approver fallback needs the roster unchanged since the request was raised (`approval_roster_snapshot` holds each member's role, standing and suspension) and answers 'members or roles changed' (a new request on the new roster is the by-design path). Not guarded: accepting an invitation that re-roles an existing member (needs that member's own credentials). Tests: `payroll-approver-guard-paths.int.test.ts`, `payroll-approver-guard-race.int.test.ts` (barrier after the check: both demotions land without the lock). Reopened run that still links a journal: `readApprovedPlan` returns its own `already_posted` blocker before the approval question. `postPayrollRunJournal` refuses a plan whose `runId` is not the run's. Tests: `tests/integration/payroll-sole-approver.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/mcp/payrollPostApprovedPlan.test.ts`, `payrollJournalPosterLock.test.ts`, `tests/unit/components/selfApprovedNote.test.tsx`.

Bank is read `?view=masked` only. Tests: `tests/unit/components/employeeReadiness*.test.ts*`, `payrollEmployeePaymentMethod.test.ts`.

- 2026-11-09 (wave 5 PS2): **payslip content** (BCEA s33(1)(b) and (g); `payslipFacts.ts`, `payslipQuantities.ts`, no migration, no calc file). Occupation, contracted hours (`hours_per_week`/`_day`) and the hourly/daily rate come from the employee's TS-a terms. Hours and days come ONLY from the run line's stored `component_breakdown` (items carrying `quantity` and `quantityUnit` 'hour'|'day', stamped at calculation time; `quantitiesFromBreakdown`), never from live assignment rows, so a FINAL slip cannot change after an assignment is edited. Ordinary hours are summed from SARS 3601 items with one unit, overtime from 3607 items with one unit; any other code is not read, and hours and days of one code are never summed (that code prints "Not recorded"). Nothing captured prints "Not recorded" (one casing); contracted hours are labelled "(contracted)", never presented as worked. Dates are `dd MMM yyyy`, money `formatMoney` (true minus printed as a hyphen: not in the PDF font). "Paid by": `EFT to FNB •••• 1234`, `Cash`, `EFT: bank details missing`, or `EFT: bank details incomplete` for a trimmed account number under 4 characters (`RIGHT(btrim(..),4)`); no pay-date line when the run has none; address parts joined only when non-empty. Still OPEN for s33(1)(g): overtime rate, Sunday/public-holiday hours, s12 averaging totals. Tests: `payslipPdf`/`payslipModel` unit, golden z10.
